{{< include ../includes/user-guide-audit.qmd >}}


::: {.feature-opalx}
`BEAM` defines the physical species and reference state for one particle
container. A typical generated distribution uses:

```opal
Beam1: BEAM, PARTICLE=ELECTRON, PC=0.1,
       NALLOC=100000, BCHARGE=1e-9, SOURCES=Sources1;
```

`BCHARGE` is normally given as a positive charge magnitude. OPALX obtains the
macroparticle sign from `CHARGE`, which defaults to the selected particle's
charge. The named emission-source list must exist when `RUN` resolves the beam.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `PARTICLE` | none | - | Selects a predefined species. If omitted, both `MASS` and `CHARGE` are required. |
| `MASS` | species value | GeV/$c^2$ | Overrides the predefined rest mass, or defines a custom species with `CHARGE`. |
| `CHARGE` | species value | $e$ | Charge in proton-charge units. It also determines the macroparticle charge sign. |
| `ENERGY` | unset | GeV | Total charged-particle energy; must exceed `MASS`. |
| `PC` | unset | GeV/$c$ | Reference momentum; must be positive. |
| `GAMMA` | unset | - | Reference Lorentz factor; must be greater than one. |
| `BCHARGE` | `0` | C | Bunch-charge magnitude used with `NALLOC` to calculate macroparticle charge. |
| `NALLOC` | required | particles | Positive allocation and macroparticle-weight baseline. Real input is converted to an integer size. |
| `SOURCES` | required | name | [`EMISSIONSOURCELIST` used by a source beam; forbidden on a beam selected as another beam's `DAUGHTERBEAM`.]{#ug-16-01} |
| `GLOBALPROCESSES` | empty | names | Uppercase array of global processes. Only `DECAY` is currently accepted. |
| `DAUGHTERBEAM` | empty | name | Beam/container that receives daughter particles from a configured decay. |
| `POLARIZATION` | unset | - | [Muon-only vector `{Px, Py, Pz}` with $|\mathbf P|\leq1$; requires `PARTICLE`. Setting it, including to zero, enables spin tracking. Every particle starts with this vector, given along the same axes as the distribution momenta.]{#ug-16-02} |
| `BCURRENT`, `BFREQ` | unset | - | [Legacy attributes explicitly rejected by OPALX; use `BCHARGE`.]{#ug-16-03} |

[The additional `TUNEINITIAL` array supplies repeated triples `{kinetic_energy_GeV, radius_m, radial_momentum_mc, ...}` to the experimental `RUN,SPECTRALTUNES=TRUE` diagnostic. It does not replace the ordinary source distribution. See [Tune Calculation](cyclotron.qmd#tune-calculation).]{#ug-16-04}

The predefined `PARTICLE` values are `PHOTON`, `ELECTRON`, `POSITRON`, `MUON`,
`PION`, `PROTON`, `ANTIPROTON`, `DEUTERON`, `HMINUS`, `H2P`, `ALPHA`,
`CARBON`, `XENON`, and `URANIUM`.

## Reference energy

For generated distributions, set one of `GAMMA`, `ENERGY`, or `PC`. If more
than one is supplied, the implementation currently uses `GAMMA` before
`ENERGY`, and `ENERGY` before `PC`; relying on that precedence is discouraged.

`FROMFILE` and `EMITTEDFROMFILE` carry absolute particle momenta. A beam using
either type must omit all three reference-energy attributes. See
[Beam and Distributions](beam-distributions.qmd) for their file conventions.

## Allocation and sources

[`NALLOC` is required and must be positive. It remains the denominator used to derive macroparticle charge even when the sum of `NPARTDIST` over all sources sets a different runtime allocation. For a source beam with `N` generated particles, the total charge magnitude is `N * BCHARGE / NALLOC`; set `NALLOC=N` when the generated bunch should carry `BCHARGE`. Keep allocation and particle counts consistent unless a different weighting is intentional.]{#ug-16-05}

[**UG-16-06:** Each tracked source beam requires a non-empty `SOURCES` name. The target list must contain at least one `EMISSIONSOURCE`; it is resolved during `RUN`. A decay daughter beam receives particles only from its parent decay and must omit `SOURCES`.]{.ug-audit-other #ug-16-06}

## Multiple species, decay, and spin {#multiple-species-decay-and-spin}

Use `TRACK.BEAMS` to select several beam definitions in a fixed order. OPALX
creates one particle container per entry. For decay calculations:

- `GLOBALPROCESSES={DECAY}` is implemented for `PARTICLE=MUON` and
  `PARTICLE=PION`.
- `DAUGHTERBEAM` is optional. Without it, decayed particles are only removed.
- `DAUGHTERBEAM` must name another beam selected by the same `TRACK` command.
  A beam can be the daughter beam of only one beam, and the settings must not
  form a loop. Chains such as pion to muon to electron are allowed.
- The daughter species is fixed: a pion beam needs a `PARTICLE=MUON` daughter
  beam, and a muon beam a `PARTICLE=ELECTRON` daughter beam.
- A decay keeps the charge: the daughter beam must have the same `CHARGE` as
  its parent. The default charges are $+1$ for `PION` and $-1$ for `MUON` and
  `ELECTRON`, so set `CHARGE` where needed. For $\mu^+\to e^+$, use
  `PARTICLE=ELECTRON, CHARGE=1`; `PARTICLE=POSITRON` is rejected as a daughter.
- [A beam selected as a `DAUGHTERBEAM` must omit `GAMMA`, `ENERGY`, `PC`, and `SOURCES`. It inherits the reference particle and frame of the first source beam in its decay chain. The first entry of `TRACK.BEAMS` must be a source beam, not a decay daughter.]{#ug-16-07}
- Parent and daughter beams must represent one physical particle per
  macroparticle: `BCHARGE = NALLOC * |CHARGE| * q_e`.
- Muon decay requires `POLARIZATION`. A daughter muon beam also needs it so the
  container stores spin; the decay sets each daughter's value.

The [Decay Processes](../physics/decay-processes/index.qmd) chapter gives the
physics model and validation.

## Photon definitions

[Not yet implemented]{#ug-16-08}
Photon beams require positive `ENERGY` and `NALLOC`, and reject `MASS`,
`CHARGE`, `PC`, `GAMMA`, and `SOURCES`. [`BEAM.ENERGY` uses GeV. Photon transport is not yet available.]{#ug-16-09}
